CsvIngestResponse.description:
Response from POST /api/v1/ingest/csv (#2892).

The CSV path is the only ingest surface that computes per-row KDE
warnings, so the two extra fields live here rather than on the shared
``IngestResponse`` — the webhook endpoint would otherwise advertise a
signal it never produces.

Both fields carry defaults, so they stay out of the schema's
``required`` set: a body cached by the idempotency middleware before
this shipped (24h TTL) still validates against the new schema when it
is replayed.

WebhookCTEType.description:
CTE types accepted by the webhook endpoint.

The 7 canonical FSMA 204 CTEs (per 21 CFR 1.1310) are: harvesting,
cooling, initial_packing, first_land_based_receiving, shipping,
receiving, transformation.  GROWING is accepted for ingest
backwards-compatibility but normalizes to farm metadata, not a CTE.

parameters.description: FSMA validation mode (#1174). ``true`` (default): schema failures return HTTP 422 and nothing is persisted. ``false``: advisory — the rejection is written to the EDI rejection log (separate from the canonical FSMA stream) and the response returns ``status='rejected'`` with a rejection_id. The invalid event is NEVER inserted into the canonical ingest pipeline, so the FSMA 204 audit trail stays clean. Set only for test or migration scenarios. Global env default ``EDI_STRICT_MODE=false`` also disables strict mode.

Liveness / ingestion-posture endpoint.

Returns ``"healthy"`` when all dependencies are reachable, or
``"degraded"`` when optional dependencies (e.g. Kafka) are
unavailable.  Monitoring tools can alert on *degraded* without
treating the service as fully down.

This is deliberately shallow: ``/readiness`` (server/main.py) is the
dependency-gated probe Railway polls, and ``/health/deep`` verifies
Postgres/Neo4j/Redis connectivity.
